history.new: No collision among all factorisations of orders <= 16 (orders 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16); class counts validated against A002854 for n <= 8. Prime two-graph counts (exact for n <= 16): 1, 2, 2, 7, 14, 54, 240, 2035, 33113, ... Cancellation by [K2] is proved (CLM-C14-07c). The Skeptic notes that this evidence was thin - up to order 16 almost every composite is [K2] (x) X, covered by the proved cancellation - and extends it substantially: all 53,703 multisets of prime classes with <= 8 vertices and product order <= 64, screened by exact integer power sums tr((S+I)^k) and decided by exact switching-equivalence tests (2,205 cospectral groups, 3,012 pairs), give 0 collisions.

history.new: Low confidence. The product of two-graphs is the Kronecker product of the matrices S + I, as used for graphical Hadamard matrices (Abiad-Butler-Haemers, arXiv:1801.01149 sections 4-5). Cancellation by [K_2] is Oh-Yoo-Yun (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2013). No unique-factorisation statement for two-graphs, or for +-1 matrices up to signed permutation similarity, was found. Lajou's unique factorisation of signed graphs concerns the Cartesian product (Historian audit 2026-10-19, reviews/historian_C11_C20.md).

statement:
Every switching class of finite graphs has a unique factorisation into prime switching classes with respect
to the product induced by the symmetric difference (equivalently, symmetric +-1 matrices with unit diagonal
up to signed permutation similarity, under the Kronecker product).
title: H-C14-4: two-graphs form a free commutative monoid under the symmetric-difference (Kronecker) product
